drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Attached are our initial comments to the draft Share Purchase Agreement. We have tightened the closing mechanics, expanded the seller representations to cover authority/title/no-conflict matters, and clarified that the indemnity applies to breaches, pre-closing taxes, undisclosed liabilities, and fraud/willful misconduct. We have left the Purchase Price as a bracketed placeholder for the parties’ business teams to confirm.

Please let us know if Buyer has any issue with these concepts, and we can work through the indemnity thresholds and any survival periods in the next turn.

Best,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: PARTIES. This Share Purchase Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into by and between the Seller and Meridian Acquisitions LLC, a limited liability company, as buyer (the “Buyer”). Seller and Buyer are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.”
edits.name: Parties clause

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, at Closing the Buyer shall purchase from the Seller, and the Seller shall sell to the Buyer, all of the Shares, free and clear of all liens, claims, pledges, security interests, restrictions, options, rights of first refusal, and other encumbrances. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares shall be USD [●] (the “Purchase Price”), payable by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by the Seller no later than two business days before Closing.
edits.name: Purchase Price

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur on the date that is five business days after satisfaction or written waiver of all conditions to Closing, and in any event no later than thirty days after signing, unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing. At Closing: (a) the Seller shall deliver duly executed instruments of transfer for the Shares and all other documents reasonably required to vest good and marketable title to the Shares in Buyer; and (b) Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price in accordance with Section 1.
edits.name: Closing mechanics

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. The Seller represents and warrants to Buyer that: (a) Seller has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) this Agreement constitutes a valid and binding obligation of Seller, enforceable against Seller in accordance with its terms; (c) Seller owns the Shares beneficially and of record, free and clear of all liens, claims, pledges, security interests, restrictions, options, rights of first refusal, and other encumbrances; (d) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by Seller do not conflict with or violate any agreement, organizational document, law, order, or obligation applicable to Seller or the Shares; (e) the financial statements delivered to Buyer are accurate in all material respects, have been prepared in accordance with applicable accounting standards consistently applied, and fairly present the financial condition and results of operations of the applicable business for the periods covered; and (f) Seller has not omitted any fact necessary to make the information provided to Buyer, taken as a whole, not misleading in any material respect.
edits.name: Seller representations

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. From and after Closing, the Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, successors, and assigns, from and against all losses, liabilities, damages, claims, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, arising out of or relating to: (a) any breach of Seller’s representations, warranties, covenants, or obligations under this Agreement; (b) any liabilities of the Company or relating to the Shares to the extent arising from facts, events, or periods before Closing and not disclosed in writing to Buyer before signing; (c) any pre-Closing taxes; and (d) fraud, intentional misrepresentation, or willful misconduct. The indemnification rights in this Section are cumulative and do not limit any other rights or remedies available at law, in equity, or under this Agreement.
edits.name: Indemnity

Opposing counsel’s requested uncapped indemnity for fundamental/title/tax/undisclosed liabilities and fraud was largely incorporated, but I added survival periods, written claim procedures, mitigation/no-duplication language, and a reasonableness/good-faith constraint on Buyer’s diligence condition so Closing is not subject to an unfettered walk right. drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Attached are Seller’s Round 2 revisions. We have accepted the core allocation Buyer requested for fundamental/title, taxes, undisclosed pre-Closing liabilities, and fraud/willful misconduct, including no basket or cap for those categories and express preservation of equitable/statutory remedies.

To keep the draft administrable, we added customary survival and claim procedures, plus no-duplication and mitigation language. We also included Buyer’s requested clean-title deliverables and diligence condition, but framed diligence satisfaction as good-faith, reasonable satisfaction and tied the deliverables to those reasonably necessary to transfer clean title to the Shares.

The Purchase Price remains bracketed pending principal-level business confirmation.

Best,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.name: Purchase Price

edits.text: 2. CLOSING; CONDITIONS. Closing shall occur on the date that is five business days after satisfaction or written waiver of all conditions to Closing, and in any event no later than thirty days after signing, unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing. Buyer’s obligation to consummate the Closing is conditioned upon: (a) Buyer’s completion of final confirmatory diligence to its reasonable satisfaction, exercised in good faith; (b) Seller’s delivery of duly executed instruments of transfer for the Shares and all other transfer documents reasonably necessary to vest good and marketable title to the Shares in Buyer; (c) Seller’s delivery of any third-party consents required for the transfer of the Shares; and (d) Seller’s delivery of payoff letters, lien releases, UCC termination authorizations, or similar evidence reasonably necessary to deliver the Shares free and clear of all liens, claims, pledges, security interests, restrictions, options, rights of first refusal, and other encumbrances. At Closing: (i) the Seller shall deliver the items described in this Section 2; and (ii) Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price in accordance with Section 1.
edits.name: Closing; Conditions

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. From and after Closing, the Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, successors, and assigns, from and against all losses, liabilities, damages, claims, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, arising out of or relating to: (a) any breach of Seller’s representations, warranties, covenants, or obligations under this Agreement; (b) any liabilities of the Company or relating to the Shares to the extent arising from facts, events, or periods before Closing and not disclosed in writing to Buyer before signing; (c) any pre-Closing taxes; and (d) fraud, intentional misrepresentation, or willful misconduct. No basket, deductible, de minimis threshold, cap, or other monetary limitation shall apply to claims arising out of or relating to fundamental representations, title to the Shares, taxes, undisclosed liabilities described in clause (b), fraud, intentional misrepresentation, or willful misconduct. Seller’s representations and warranties shall survive Closing for eighteen months; provided that fundamental representations, representations concerning title to the Shares, tax matters, undisclosed liabilities described in clause (b), and claims based on fraud, intentional misrepresentation, or willful misconduct shall survive until sixty days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Any indemnification claim must be asserted by written notice describing in reasonable detail the basis for the claim and the estimated amount of losses, if then known, before expiration of the applicable survival period; any claim so timely asserted shall survive until finally resolved. The indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate losses and shall not recover more than once for the same loss. The indemnification rights in this Section are cumulative and do not limit any other rights or remedies available at law, in equity, or under this Agreement, including equitable or statutory remedies.
edits.name: Indemnity
